argument:
CLAIM: development choice comes from the card pool, so the weapon's job is to be a cheap, legible route into that pool, and today most weapon Disciplines are too shallow to be a route while two Disciplines carry no cards at all.

ARITHMETIC 1, the economy that makes a route worthwhile. A career to level 10 spends 32 DP (18:63) and gains exactly 3 Discipline ranks, at levels 3, 6 and 9. Starting ranks are always rank 1 (08:100). Rank cost is tiered by Discipline: the five melee weapon Disciplines cost 1/2/4, Archery costs 2/4/8, Animal 3/6/12, and the twelve others 4/8/16 (05:67-79). The cumulative cost of reaching rank r is 1/3/7 for the cheap tier and 2/6/14 for Archery. Cards cost 2/4/8 (08:145-148). So a complete weapon identity, meaning rank 3 plus a Novice, an Adept and a Master card, costs 7+2+4+8 = 21 of 32 DP for Blades, Axes, Polearms, Heavy Weapon or Unarmed, and 14+14 = 28 of 32 for Archery. Archery, not the melee group, is the expensive weapon, and the melee ladder is already priced as the cheapest entry in the game (05:72), which is the shape a route should have.

ARITHMETIC 2, the depth ledger, recomputed this round and shown as rank-1/rank-2/rank-3 attributions with pool = r1+r2+r3. Base A is the 177 discipline-gated cards in 09/11/12. Base B adds the 85 gated class-ability rows in 05-classes.qmd, 262 gated cards in total; a further 45 header cards carry no discipline requirement.

Fire 2/2/0 pool 4 (base B 8/2/0 pool 10)
Earth 2/5/0 pool 7 (2/5/0 pool 7)
Wind 2/4/1 pool 7 (2/4/1 pool 7)
Water 1/2/0 pool 3 (1/2/0 pool 3)
Blades 5/5/1 pool 11 (12/8/1 pool 21)
Axes 0/2/0 pool 2 (0/2/0 pool 2)
Polearms 1/2/1 pool 4 (2/2/1 pool 5)
Archery 2/2/1 pool 5 (4/2/1 pool 7)
Heavy Weapon 0/5/1 pool 6 (1/5/1 pool 7)
Unarmed 2/1/1 pool 4 (4/1/1 pool 6)
Protection 4/5/0 pool 9 (16/10/0 pool 26)
Armor 3/1/0 pool 4 (7/3/0 pool 10)
Animal 1/0/0 pool 1 (3/1/0 pool 4)
Plants 1/5/0 pool 6 (4/5/0 pool 9)
Energy 11/8/2 pool 21 (22/14/3 pool 39)
Life 1/7/0 pool 8 (4/7/0 pool 11)
Religion 4/5/3 pool 12 (7/5/3 pool 15)
Mind 9/4/2 pool 15 (18/5/2 pool 25)
Summon 0/0/0 pool 0 (0/0/0 pool 0)
Fate 0/0/0 pool 0 (0/0/0 pool 0)
Stealth 3/0/0 pool 3 (11/2/0 pool 13)
Sleight 2/0/0 pool 2 (9/0/0 pool 9)
Lore 1/0/0 pool 1 (5/2/0 pool 7)
Tactics 13/2/0 pool 15 (20/6/0 pool 26)

Two reconciliation notes for the editor. First, the charter's own list, Axes 2, Polearms 4, Water 3, Animal 4, Blades 10, Protection 26, is measured on two different bases: Axes, Polearms and Water are base A figures, Animal, Protection and Sleight are base B figures, and Blades is 11 on base A and 21 on base B, never 10. The ledger above is the reproducible version. Second, Summon and Fate are zero on both bases: not a shallow route, no route at all, while both are listed as core Disciplines (08:54-55) and both appear as a grouped requirement in the Esoteric group (22:234).

ARITHMETIC 3, the coverage standard as a bill. The owner's rule has three parts and each is countable. (a) Entry: rank 1 is what every starting grant hands out (08:100), so a Discipline with no rank-1 card is a locked door. Four fail on base A: Axes 0, Heavy Weapon 0, Summon 0, Fate 0. (b) Depth: every Discipline should have a rank 2. Six fail on base A: Animal, Lore, Sleight, Stealth, Summon, Fate. (c) Cap: a missing rank 3 is acceptable only if the Discipline is used as a single-rank requirement in many cards. Price it: a Master card costs 8 DP, or four Novice cards, so many is set at four rank-1 cards. On base A, 15 of 24 Disciplines have no rank-3 card; 2 of those already clear the bar on breadth alone, Protection with 4 rank-1 cards and Tactics with 13, and 13 do not: Fire, Earth, Water, Axes, Armor, Animal, Plants, Life, Summon, Fate, Stealth, Sleight, Lore. Each of the 13 then needs either a rank-3 card or one more rank-1 card, and the cheapest correct fix is 13 rank-1 cards, one per Discipline. Base A bill: 4 entry + 6 rank-2 + 13 breadth = 23 cards, which lifts every Discipline clear of all three rules. On base B the same rules cost 12 cards (3 entry: Axes, Summon, Fate; 3 rank-2: Summon, Fate, Sleight; 6 breadth: Earth, Water, Axes, Animal, Summon, Fate), so counting class abilities as cards saves 11 cards of the bill. That 23 against 12 is the arithmetic value of the existing class-ability spine.

ARITHMETIC 4, which weapon routes are too shallow to carry identity. Six weapon Disciplines, pools on base A: Blades 11, Heavy Weapon 6, Archery 5, Polearms 4, Unarmed 4, Axes 2. Apply a route floor of two cards at each rung, that is a pool of 6 as the point where a ladder can be climbed at all: Blades 0 more, Heavy Weapon 0, Archery 1, Unarmed 2, Polearms 2, Axes 4, a bill of 9 cards. Apply instead parity with the Disciplines that do carry a rank 3, whose pools are 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 15 and 21 with a median of 7 (Polearms 4, Unarmed 4, Archery 5, Heavy Weapon 6, Wind 7, Blades 11, Religion 12, Mind 15, Energy 21): Heavy Weapon 1, Archery 2, Unarmed 3, Polearms 3, Axes 5, Blades 0, a bill of 14 cards. Three defects make the shallow routes fail now rather than later. First, the cheapest recipes point at the shallowest pools: 1 Blades has 5 entries and 1 Archery has 2, while 1 Axes has none, so the Handaxe (15:177) and the Mace (15:180) are keys that open nothing until the hero has spent one of only three rank picks in a career. Second, every rank-3 weapon card is also a multi-Discipline capstone: Cyclone 3 Blades; Sunshot 3 Archery and 1 Tactics and 1 Stealth; Harvest the Fear 3 Polearms and 1 Tactics and 1 Mind; Groundbreaker 3 Heavy Weapon and 1 Tactics and 1 Unarmed; Taken Alive 3 Unarmed and 1 Tactics and 1 Armor (09:236, 09:533, 09:542, 09:551, 09:560). Each costs five ranks in total and four of the five route through Tactics, so the weapon ladder terminates outside itself; and because rank 3 requires the picks at levels 3 and 6, none of them is legal before level 6. Axes has no cap card at all, so its ladder stops at rank 2. Third, a route that is identical for two weapons is not an identity: the tree is 17 weapons on 12 distinct recipes (15:171), with Dagger and Shortsword both 1 Blades, Spear and Halberd both 1 Polearms, and the bows all 1 Archery (15:173-186). The space is free: three ranks across six weapon Disciplines offers 4^6 minus 1, that is 4095 distinct non-empty recipes, and the tree uses 12.

ARITHMETIC 5, the total bill. Union on base A: 23 coverage cards plus 14 parity cards, minus 1 shared card, since the Axes entry card is also one of its five, is 36 cards. The minimum reading, coverage plus the floor-of-6 rule, is 23 plus 9 minus 1, that is 31 cards. The bottom of the ledger is Summon and Fate: zero cards at any rank, in any chapter, on either base. Each needs an entry card, a rank-2 card, and either a cap or one more rank-1 card for breadth, three cards each and six for the pair, to stop being words in the Discipline table. That is the owner's standard applied to the whole spine: every Discipline an entry, every Discipline a rank 2, and breadth or a cap to finish, with the weapon Disciplines funded to 6 or 14 cards on the way.

evidence.claim: The price and legality table that sets the card economy a route must fit inside.
A Master card costs 8 DP, the unit used to price the breadth offset.
The whole career budget: 32 DP and three rank picks.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Total DP by level 10: 32. Total Discipline ranks gained: 3 (levels 3, 6 and 9).

evidence.claim: Rank cost is tiered by Discipline, so entry price is part of identity.
The melee weapon ladder is the cheapest tier at 1/2/4, against 4/8/16 for most others.
Archery costs 2/4/8, so the ranged weapon route is the expensive one.
Entry rung is rank 1, so a Discipline with no rank-1 card cannot be entered.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Starting Disciplines from ancestry, culture, and class are always rank 1.

evidence.claim: The weapon tree is already written as Discipline recipes, the basis for reading a weapon as a route.
Dagger: 1 Blades.
Shortsword carries the identical recipe as the Dagger, so the recipe alone does not distinguish them.
The Handaxe's 1 Axes points at a pool that contains no rank-1 Axes card, a key that opens nothing.
The Mace's 1 Heavy Weapon points at a pool with no rank-1 card on base A.
The Maul is the only 3 Heavy Weapon recipe, so the deepest Heavy Weapon route buys exactly one printed card.
The book already separates holding the object from owning the cards, which is what a route means.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: wielding a kit weapon does not grant the maneuvers that require them.

evidence.claim: Fate is a core Discipline with a stated identity, and it carries zero cards in the entire spine.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Luck, chance, destiny, oaths kept and broken, the turning of a moment

evidence.claim: Summon and Fate appear only as a grouped requirement, never as a card's own Discipline.
Animal's single base-A card: a whole Discipline carried by one divine spell.
Groundbreaker: the deepest Heavy Weapon recipe and a multi-Discipline capstone.
Taken Alive: the deepest Unarmed recipe, again routed through Tactics.
The class chapter states the law directly: prerequisites plus level are the real gate.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Their real gate is Discipline prerequisites and level (Adept at 3, Master at 7).
